reports.title: Obesity links to inosine, ENT1 variants, supplements, and tourniquet occlusion
reports.summary: This community covers obesity as a shared outcome or exposure across three papers: inosine and ENT1 in brown fat, dietary supplement use among cancer survivors, and tourniquet use in school-age emergencies. The two brown-fat papers agree that inosine and ENT1 reduce obesity, with C1 stating that inosine counteracts obesity and C4 reporting that ENT1 ablation counteracted diet-induced obesity in mice, while C5 reports only an association for the Ile216Thr variant. C2 reports that obesity was associated with lower dietary supplement use, an association rather than a causal link. C3 reports that the 3-turn tourniquet maximum was not adequate in some obese, older subjects, and it is associated with arterial occlusion. Press coverage matched only C1, which press releases understated (press 1 vs paper 3), and C3, which was aligned; the other three claims had no press match. No papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Inosine, released during apoptosis, counteracts obesity by regulating thermogenic fat, a finding press releases understated.
Pharmacological inhibition and genetic ablation of ENT1 in mice enhanced brown adipose tissue activity and counteracted diet-induced obesity.
The Ile216Thr loss-of-function variant in human ENT1 is associated with lower body mass index and lower odds of obesity.
Obesity is associated with lower dietary supplement use among individuals living with and beyond breast, prostate, and colorectal cancer.
The 3-turn tourniquet maximum was not adequate in some obese, older subjects, an association with arterial occlusion that press releases matched.

reports.title: Probiotics and hot water immersion effects on glucose metabolism
reports.summary: The findings study interventions that may affect glucose metabolism: probiotic supplementation in a PBDE exposure model (P1) and hot water immersion in sedentary overweight adults (P2). Both papers report a decrease in glucose metabolism using conditional causal wording ("may"), so they do not conflict. P1 is a rodent-style exposure study linked to gut microbiome changes, while P2 is a human intervention study with fasting glucose and insulin outcomes. Press coverage of both papers was labelled aligned, meaning the press statements matched the papers' strength. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Probiotic supplementation may decrease glucose metabolism disruption linked to PBDE-induced reprogramming, in association with gut microbial changes.
Hot water immersion may decrease glucose metabolism, with reductions in fasting glucose and insulin after chronic intervention.

reports.title: β3-adrenergic receptor overexpression, premature menopause, and heart failure outcomes
reports.summary: These papers study heart failure as the shared outcome, with β3-adrenergic receptor overexpression and premature menopause as exposures, plus one study of miR-19a/19b expression in heart failure patients. The β3AR studies (P1) report that overexpression was associated with decreased heart failure in mice, and the paper's own wording is causal, so the findings are direct causal statements in animal models. The menopause study (P2) reports that premature menopause may increase heart failure risk, with a graded association across menopausal ages. Press coverage of the β3AR findings was aligned in one case and understated in two, while press statements on the menopause findings were aligned or absent; no retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Transgenic overexpression of β3AR in the heart was reported to decrease congestive heart failure in mice subjected to aortic stenosis.
AAV9-mediated β3AR overexpression in wild-type mice at late disease stages was reported to reverse the heart failure phenotype.
Premature menopause may increase the risk of heart failure, with women having a history of premature menopause showing higher heart failure risk than those without.
Risk of heart failure was reported to increase as age at menopause decreased, with a significant trend across menopausal age groups.
Expression of miR-19a/19b was reported to be associated with increased heart failure in patients.

reports.title: Pain, depressive symptoms, sleep problems and quality of life across diverse conditions
reports.summary: These claims span neurological, psychiatric, oncologic, menopausal, and gastroenterological studies, linked by pain, depressive symptoms, sleep problems, and quality of life. Several papers report positive associations, such as pain with depressive symptoms and insomnia with lower quality of life, while others report null results, such as no link between ALSFRS-R score and quality of life. The buprenorphine/samidorphan trials conflict: FORWARD-5 reported lower depressive symptom scores than placebo, while FORWARD-4 did not reach its primary endpoint. Press releases matched 11 of 26 claims; 4 were labeled overstated (for medical cannabis and non-motor symptoms in ALS) and 10 aligned with the paper, and no paper in this set is retracted.

key_findings.text: Medical cannabis was reported to reduce cancer-related pain in registry data, with the press overstating this relative to the paper.
Non-motor symptoms in ALS and genitourinary syndrome of menopause were reported to decrease quality of life.
Buprenorphine/samidorphan reduced depressive symptoms versus placebo in FORWARD-5, but FORWARD-4 found no significant effect on depressive symptoms.
Insomnia was associated with more depressive symptoms and lower quality of life, and pain was associated with higher depressive symptom scores.

Several relationships were null: ALSFRS-R score showed no correlation with quality of life or PHQ-9, cannabidiol showed no quality of life difference from placebo, and an emotional processing intervention produced no change in secondary outcomes.

reports.title: Younger age and associations with abortion beliefs and intracerebral hemorrhage lesions
reports.summary: Both claims in this community link younger age to an outcome, but the outcomes differ: belief that abortion is illegal in one paper and detection of an underlying structural lesion in another. Each paper's wording is correlational (strength 1), so both are described as associations rather than causal effects. The two papers do not conflict, since neither reports a null or opposite-direction result. Press coverage was matched for only the intracerebral hemorrhage finding, which was aligned with its paper, while the abortion finding had no press match.

key_findings.text: Younger age is associated with belief that abortion is illegal.
Younger age is associated with detection of an underlying structural lesion in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.
Press coverage of the intracerebral hemorrhage finding was aligned with the paper's strength, while the abortion finding had no matched press statement.

reports.title: Thigh intramuscular fat and cannabis: adverse events and cancer pain
reports.summary: This community groups two unrelated studies that share adverse events as an outcome: thigh intramuscular fat in nonischemic cardiomyopathy and medical cannabis in cancer-related pain. The thigh fat study reports that thigh intramuscular fat was associated with adverse events, and that the high-fat group had a higher risk. The cannabis registry reports that medical cannabis was associated with no effect on adverse events. The two papers do not conflict because they study different exposures. Press coverage of the two claims that had a press match was aligned with the paper strengths, and one thigh fat claim had no press match.

key_findings.text: Thigh intramuscular fat was associated with adverse events in patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy.
Medical cannabis was associated with no effect on adverse events in patients with cancer-related pain.

reports.title: Thigh fat and liver fibrosis stage versus cardiac events
reports.summary: This community covers two exposures, thigh intramuscular fat and liver fibrosis stage, both examined against cardiac events. In patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and reduced ejection fraction, thigh intramuscular fat may increase cardiac events (P1). In adults with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, no association was found between fibrosis stage and cardiac events (P2). The two findings study different exposures in different populations, so they do not directly contradict each other. No press statements were matched to either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Thigh intramuscular fat may increase cardiac events in patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and reduced ejection fraction.
No association was found between fibrosis stage and cardiac events in adults with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

reports.title: Hepatic steatosis and reduced amino acid catabolism and urea production
reports.summary: These claims study how hepatic steatosis (fatty liver) relates to amino acid catabolism and urea production, mainly in glucagon-related liver studies, with one separate claim on steatosis and bone trabecular attenuation. All six claims report a decrease in the outcome, so no findings conflict in direction. The paper that reports the strongest wording says hepatic steatosis may impair glucagon-dependent enhancement of amino acid catabolism, while the other claims use associational wording. No press statements were matched to any claim, so press coverage cannot be compared with these findings.

key_findings.text: Hepatic steatosis may impair glucagon-dependent enhancement of amino acid catabolism.
Steatosis was associated with lower amino acid clearance and reduced urea production in mice and cultured hepatocytes.
Glucagon-induced ureagenesis was associated with impairment in perfused rat livers with hepatic steatosis.
Genes for amino acid catabolism were associated with downregulation in mice with hepatic steatosis and in mice lacking the glucagon receptor.
Hepatic steatosis was associated with low trabecular attenuation in an AI analysis of lung cancer screening CTs.

reports.title: Visual impairment, cognition, aging, and COVID-19 vaccine antibody responses
reports.summary: The claims cover several unrelated topics: visual impairment and cognitive function, antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccines and infection, age-related markers in cats and humans, exercise and cognition, and migraine treatment initiation. Papers on visual impairment report associations in both directions with cognitive decline, with one paper calling vision loss the likely driving force. For vaccines, the booster papers agree that BNT162b2 boosters increased antibody responses, while age showed no effect on third-dose responses but was linked to higher neutralizing titers in another study. Of the 14 claims with a press match, 12 were aligned, one was understated (C1) and one was overstated (C5). The other 12 claims had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: BNT162b2 booster vaccinations increased SARS-CoV-2 antibody responses, and a fourth dose produced a further increase.
Visual impairment was associated with lower cognitive function in cross-lagged analyses, and cognitive function was associated with visual impairment in the reverse direction.
One paper states that vision loss may be the stronger driver of the association with cognitive decline than the reverse effect.
Inflammatory cytokines IL-17A and IFN-γ were inversely related to age, and neutralizing antibody titers were associated with higher age and lower IL-17A and IFN-γ.
A healthy aging education program improved cognitive functioning in older African Americans, whereas a 12-week physical activity intervention showed no effect.

reports.title: Tobacco dependence and e-referral or e-cigarette use versus smoking cessation
reports.summary: The three claims study smoking cessation through nicotine dependence, electronic referral to a tobacco quitline, and e-cigarette use for quitting. Each finding concerns whether a factor relates to quitting, and none reports a positive effect of a cessation aid. Higher nicotine dependence is associated with lower odds of quitting, while quitline e-referral and e-cigarette use show no effect on quitting. Press coverage of the quitline study included one statement that reframed its null result as an overstatement and one that matched it, the dependence finding was aligned with press coverage, and the e-cigarette finding had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Patients with high nicotine dependence were associated with a decrease in smoking cessation.
E-referral to a tobacco quitline showed no effect on quitting at 30 days or 6 months compared with general quitline callers.
Using e-cigarettes for cessation in 2017 showed no effect on successful quitting or relapse prevention.

reports.title: Anakinra outcomes and serious adverse events across unrelated treatments
reports.summary: These claims cover anakinra in severe COVID-19 with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and in Sanfilippo syndrome, direct-acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C, medical cannabis for cancer-related pain, and translumbosacral neuromodulation for fecal incontinence. The anakinra claims report associations with better respiratory function, less vasopressor need, and lower HScore in one study, and with improved neurobehavioral and functional outcomes in another. Safety claims largely agree: no serious adverse events were found for anakinra, medical cannabis, or neuromodulation, and direct-acting antiviral regimens were associated with low serious adverse event rates. No claims point in opposite directions, but the anakinra efficacy evidence comes from single studies. Press coverage was aligned with the papers for most matched claims, while the HScore claim and the Sanfilippo outcome claim were overstated.

key_findings.text: Anakinra was associated with improved respiratory function and reduced vasopressor requirement in ICU patients with severe COVID-19 and secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
No serious adverse events were found for anakinra, medical cannabis, or translumbosacral neuromodulation.
Anakinra was associated with improved neurobehavioral and functional outcomes and a multi-domain responder index improvement in Sanfilippo syndrome.
Anakinra may be beneficial for treating severe COVID-19 patients with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, according to the HScore, and larger studies are needed to validate this.
Direct-acting antiviral regimens were associated with low short-term rates of serious adverse events in hepatitis C treatment studies.

reports.title: Type 2 diabetes, cognition, lipids, and gut disorders across eight studies
reports.summary: These findings cover type 2 diabetes and related exposures and outcomes, including gastrointestinal disorders, cognition after stroke, postpartum dyslipidemia, and bowel disease treatments, drawn from eight papers. Type 2 diabetes is associated with several gastrointestinal disorders (C9, C13), but the same genetic study reports no association with inflammatory bowel disease (C1). Type 2 diabetes is associated with poorer global cognition after stroke (C3, C15), while impaired fasting glucose showed no difference (C11). Exercise is associated with cognitive gains in one trial (C4, C12, C16), and opioid delta-receptor agonists may ameliorate IBS-like symptoms (C8). Press labels were aligned 11 times, overstated 6 times, and understated once, with overstatement seen for the bowel transplant result (C6) and the exercise trend (C4).

key_findings.text: Type 2 diabetes is associated with peptic ulcer disease, irritable bowel syndrome, gastritis-duodenitis, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticular disease through positive genetic correlation.
No association was found between type 2 diabetes and inflammatory bowel disease.
Mendelian randomisation analyses suggest that type 2 diabetes may causally affect peptic ulcer disease and gastritis-duodenitis, and may be bidirectionally related to gastroesophageal reflux disease.
Type 2 diabetes is associated with poorer global cognition after stroke, while impaired fasting glucose showed no significant difference.
Underlying dyslipidemia is associated with type 2 diabetes in women after a recent gestational diabetes pregnancy, and endogenous lipogenesis may be a driving force for diabetes onset.

reports.title: Physical activity links to brain, lung, and cancer outcomes; mixed unrelated treatments
reports.summary: The claims cover physical activity against brain structure, lung function, and cancer outcomes, plus several unrelated treatment and biomarker studies. Brain and lung papers mostly report associations of physical activity with larger brain volumes, cortical thickness, and higher FEV1 and FVC, while one lung paper found no link to lung function decline. In cancer, the colorectal study found no significant overall survival association but reported links to progression-free survival and fewer serious adverse events, and the breast cancer study associated activity with lower recurrence and mortality. Of 25 claims, 15 matched a press statement: 15 aligned, 3 overstated (C3, C5, C13), and 1 understated (C4), and the overstated C3 is a null overall survival result. No papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Physical activity is associated with larger brain volumes, gray matter density, and cortical thickness, strongest in motor regions, and one paper suggests it may benefit brain health.
Physical activity is associated with higher FEV1 and FVC in a prospective cohort, but no association was found for lung function decline.
Meeting physical activity guidelines around breast cancer diagnosis is associated with reduced recurrence and mortality.

In metastatic colorectal cancer, physical activity showed no statistically significant association with overall survival, while it was associated with longer progression-free survival and lower risk of grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events.
Atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel prolonged progression-free survival in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, including the PD-L1-positive subgroup.

reports.title: Metformin, titin stiffness, and heart function; miR-19a and vagal activity
reports.summary: This community covers metformin's effects on cardiac stiffness, diastolic function, delirium, and mortality, along with separate papers on miR-19a/19b after myocardial infarction and cardiac vagal activity during exercise. The mouse study (P1) reports that metformin lowers left ventricular passive stiffness and improves diastolic function, with an association for exercise capacity and a null result for PEVK phosphorylation alongside an association for N2B phosphorylation. A retrospective cohort (P2) reports that metformin may lower delirium and mortality risk, a conditional claim. Press coverage was aligned for four claims, overstated for three (including the delirium and mortality and exercise capacity claims), and understated for two (the vagal activity claim and the HFpEF stiffness claim).

key_findings.text: Metformin lowers left ventricular passive stiffness and improves diastolic function in HFpEF-like mice, with the stiffness reduction attributed to increased titin compliance.
Metformin may lower the risk of delirium and mortality in patients with diabetes mellitus.
miR-19a/19b reduces myocardial infarction-induced cardiac damage and protects cardiac function in mice.
Cardiac vagal nerve activity increases during exercise and is crucial for maintaining cardiac function.

Metformin is associated with preserved exercise capacity, while the paper found no association between metformin and PEVK phosphorylation, and found an association between metformin and increased N2B phosphorylation.

reports.title: JWH-018 and cardiac vagal denervation effects on heart rate
reports.summary: These findings cover two unrelated exposures, each linked to heart rate: the synthetic cannabinoid JWH-018 and cardiac vagal denervation. The community contains two papers and two claims, both at direct causal strength. The two claims point in opposite directions, but they concern different exposures, so they do not conflict with each other. Neither claim matched a press release, so press coverage cannot be compared for this community.

key_findings.text: JWH-018 increased heart rate within the first hour of acute dosing.
Cardiac vagal denervation decreased heart rate during exercise.

reports.title: Adiposity, bariatric surgery, and iron therapy with myocardial infarction and cancer outcomes
reports.summary: These findings study adiposity measures and myocardial infarction risk, bariatric surgery and its effects on weight, glycemia, and cancer outcomes, and high-dose intravenous iron and myocardial infarction. The UK Biobank adiposity study associates BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio and waist-to-height ratio with MI risk, with waist-to-hip ratio and waist circumference showing a larger excess risk in women. Bariatric surgery is associated with lower cancer-related mortality and obesity-associated cancer incidence in the 10-year trial, and with weight and glycemic improvements in adolescents, though the adolescent comparison reports a null-to-positive contrast for BMI in the TODAY arm. Press coverage overstated the bariatric surgery findings in several cases, while the iron trial was reported as understated by one press release and aligned by another. Press coverage of the adiposity and MI findings was aligned where matched, and most claims had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: High-dose intravenous iron was reported to reduce myocardial infarction compared with reactive low-dose iron in haemodialysis patients.
Bariatric surgery was associated with lower cancer-related mortality and lower incidence of obesity-associated cancer over 10 years, with press coverage overstating these findings.
Waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and general and central adiposity were associated with increased myocardial infarction risk, with a greater excess risk for waist measures in women.
Bariatric surgery in severely obese adolescents with type 2 diabetes was associated with reduced body weight, better glycemic control, and improved comorbidities compared with medical therapy.

Body mass index and obesity-related cancer risk were associated with increasing BMI in a pooled European cohort, and waist-to-hip ratio was more strongly associated with MI than BMI in the UK Biobank study.

reports.title: Blood pressure, fitness, bariatric surgery and cardiovascular risk outcomes
reports.summary: These findings study blood pressure, cardiorespiratory fitness, cannabis use disorder, bariatric surgery, inspiratory muscle training and albuminuria in relation to cardiovascular disease outcomes. Several papers agree that higher systolic blood pressure and low cardiorespiratory fitness are each associated with increased cardiovascular mortality risk. The directions conflict across exposures: bariatric surgery and inspiratory muscle training are associated with decreases, while cannabis use disorder and medical therapy for type 2 diabetes are associated with increases. Press coverage matched seven claims, with six labeled aligned and two labeled overstated (one claim carries both labels), and five claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: Higher systolic blood pressure is associated with increased cardiovascular disease mortality risk.
Low cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, and high fitness may attenuate but does not eliminate the added risk linked to high systolic blood pressure.

Metabolic bariatric surgery was associated with a reduction in estimated cardiovascular event risk, whereas medical therapy was associated with an increase among adolescents with type 2 diabetes and severe obesity.
Cannabis use disorder is associated with an increased rate of incident adverse cardiovascular events (RR 1.57).

Inspiratory muscle strength training is associated with lower systolic blood pressure in older adults with obstructive sleep apnea, and higher systolic blood pressure is associated with greater albuminuria prevalence.

reports.title: Renal cell carcinoma linked to kinase activity and excess body weight
reports.summary: This community covers renal cell carcinoma as the outcome, with kinase pathway activity and excess body weight as the exposures studied. The kinase profiling study (P1) reports that renal cell carcinoma is associated with increased PI3K pathway activity and increased Src family kinase activity. The pooled European cohort study (P2) reports that excess body weight is associated with increased renal cell carcinoma risk. All three claims show an increase direction, so no opposing directions or null results appear here. Press coverage was aligned with the paper's wording for the PI3K claim (C1) and the body weight claim (C2), while the Src family kinase claim (C3) had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Renal cell carcinoma is associated with increased phosphoinositide-3-kinase pathway activity in the kinase profiling study (P1).
Excess body weight is associated with increased risk of renal cell carcinoma in the pooled European cohort study (P2).
Renal cell carcinoma is associated with increased Src family kinase activity in the kinase profiling study (P1), with no matched press statement.

reports.title: Maternal exposures and preterm birth outcomes in pregnancy
reports.summary: The findings study maternal exposures during pregnancy, including H1N1 influenza ICU admission, interpregnancy interval, and residence change in the first trimester, against preterm birth and related adverse birth outcomes. P1 reports that ICU admission for 2009 H1N1 influenza was associated with preterm birth, and P3 reports that moving in the first trimester was associated with preterm birth. P2 reports no association found between short interpregnancy intervals and preterm birth. The two positive associations are both correlational and do not conflict with the null result, which concerns a different exposure. All three claims are labelled aligned with their press coverage, so press statements matched the strength of the papers' wording. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Moving during the first trimester was associated with preterm birth, low birth weight, and small for gestational age.
ICU admission for 2009 H1N1 influenza was associated with preterm birth, low birth weight, and low Apgar scores.
No association found between short interpregnancy intervals under 12 months and preterm birth.

reports.title: Maternal influenza ICU stays and moving linked to low birth weight
reports.summary: These findings cover maternal exposures during pregnancy, namely ICU admission for 2009 H1N1 influenza and residential moves in the first trimester, and their link to birth outcomes, mainly low birth weight. Both claims report a positive association at strength 1 ('associated with'), so the papers do not conflict. The second paper's wording also mentions preterm birth as associated with first-trimester moves. Press releases matched both claims as aligned, so neither was overstated or understated relative to the paper. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Maternal ICU admission for 2009 H1N1 influenza is associated with low birth weight.
Residential moves during the first trimester of pregnancy are associated with low birth weight.
Press coverage of both papers' low birth weight findings was aligned with the strength of the papers' wording.

reports.title: Pregnancy exposures (influenza, interpregnancy interval, residence moves) and adverse birth outcomes
reports.summary: These three papers study maternal exposures during pregnancy, namely influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 infection, short interpregnancy interval after a stillbirth, and residential change in the first trimester, and their links to adverse birth outcomes. The influenza paper reports an association with adverse birth outcomes (C1), and the residence-change paper says moving in the first trimester may be a risk factor (C3). The interpregnancy interval paper found no association with adverse outcomes (C2), a null result that differs from the two positive findings but does not contradict them because it concerns a different exposure. None of the three claims has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers.

key_findings.text: Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 infection during pregnancy is associated with adverse birth outcomes.
Residential mobility during the first trimester of pregnancy may increase the risk of adverse birth outcomes.
No association found between a short interpregnancy interval after a stillbirth and adverse birth outcomes.

reports.title: Exercise, diet, sleep, distress and employment-linked outcomes across six studies
reports.summary: These findings study exercise, diet quality, sleep problems, employment disruption and psychological distress, drawn from six papers. Every claim is correlational (strength 1), so each relationship is reported as associated with the exposure rather than causal. Exercise is linked to higher Gdf15 expression in mouse tissues and to higher cardiac vagal nerve activity, and 20 minutes or more of exercise is linked to lower distress scores. Diet quality is linked to lunch type, and a mild negative correlation is reported between diet quality and distress, with no conflicting directions reported across papers. Three claims have press matches, all labelled aligned, while eight claims have no press match and cannot be compared; no retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Exercise is associated with increased Gdf15 expression in the liver, skeletal muscle and heart muscle in mice.
Homemade and staff canteen lunches are associated with higher Healthy Eating Index 2015 scores than other lunch groups.
Exercise of 20 minutes or more is associated with lower K-6 psychological distress scores than no exercise or less exercise.
Women with cancer-related employment disruption are associated with a higher burden of psychological distress, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
Exercise is associated with increased cardiac vagal nerve activity, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.

reports.title: Race and ethnicity in menarche timing and SARS-CoV-2 antibody positivity
reports.summary: This community covers two unrelated exposure-outcome pairs: race and ethnicity with age at menarche, and race and ethnicity with SARS-CoV-2 antibody positivity. The menarche paper reports a trend toward earlier menarche that was larger among participants identifying as Asian, non-Hispanic Black, or other or multiple races compared with non-Hispanic White participants, and among those self-rated with low socioeconomic status. The SARS-CoV-2 paper found no association between race/ethnicity and antibody positivity, with no significant differences between Black and Latinx participants and other race participants. No papers in this community conflict with one another because they study different outcomes. The press label for the SARS-CoV-2 finding is aligned, while the menarche finding had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Earlier menarche trends were greater among participants identifying as Asian, non-Hispanic Black, or other or multiple races compared with non-Hispanic White participants.
No association was found between race and ethnicity and SARS-CoV-2 antibody positivity.

reports.title: Low socioeconomic status and menarche timing, abortion law beliefs
reports.summary: This community groups two unrelated papers that share low socioeconomic status as an exposure, with age at menarche and belief that abortion is illegal as outcomes. The menarche paper reports that low socioeconomic status is associated with earlier age at menarche among individuals born in the US from 1950 to 2005. The abortion paper reports that low socioeconomic status is associated with believing abortion to be illegal. The two papers study different outcomes and do not conflict. Press coverage was matched to only one claim, the menarche finding, which was aligned with its paper's strength, and no press statement was matched to the abortion finding.

key_findings.text: Low socioeconomic status is associated with earlier age at menarche among individuals born in the US from 1950 to 2005.
Low socioeconomic status is associated with the belief that abortion is illegal, according to a study of women after an abortion ban.
Press coverage was matched only to the menarche finding, where press and paper strength were aligned; no press statement was matched to the abortion finding.

reports.title: Tucatinib with T-DM1 and total body irradiation: toxicity outcomes
reports.summary: This community covers two unrelated interventions, tucatinib plus ado-trastuzumab emtansine in HER2-positive breast cancer and increased total body irradiation dose in haploidentical transplantation, each linked to treatment-related toxicity. The two papers do not conflict because they study different exposures in different settings. The tucatinib finding is conditional: the paper's wording describes acceptable toxicity and preliminary antitumor activity in heavily pretreated patients. The total body irradiation finding is a null result, with no association found between increased dose and treatment-related toxicity. The only press-matched claim is overstated, with press coverage at strength 3 against the paper's strength 2, and the total body irradiation claim had no press match.

key_findings.text: Tucatinib plus ado-trastuzumab emtansine may be linked to acceptable treatment-related toxicity in heavily pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients.
No association was found between increased total body irradiation and treatment-related toxicity in haploidentical transplantation for severe haemoglobinopathies.
Press coverage of the tucatinib study overstated its finding relative to the paper's own conditional wording.

reports.title: Tucatinib and Rucaparib Antitumor Activity in HER2 Breast and BRCA Prostate Cancer
reports.summary: This community covers two trials of targeted treatments: tucatinib combined with ado-trastuzumab emtansine in ERBB2/HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, and rucaparib in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with BRCA1 or BRCA2 alterations. Each paper reports antitumor activity for its treatment, with the tucatinib combination worded as preliminary and rucaparib worded as direct. The two claims concern different drugs and cancers, and their coded directions differ (decrease for tucatinib, increase for rucaparib). Press coverage of the tucatinib finding was aligned with the paper, while press coverage of the rucaparib finding was aligned in one statement and overstated in another.

key_findings.text: Rucaparib increases antitumor activity in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and a deleterious BRCA alteration, with a manageable safety profile.
Tucatinib combined with ado-trastuzumab emtansine may show preliminary antitumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with ERBB2/HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.

Press coverage of the rucaparib finding was aligned with the paper in one statement and overstated relative to the paper's strength in another, while press coverage of the tucatinib finding was aligned.

reports.title: Hypertension, blood pressure control, and visual acuity with cognitive decline
reports.summary: These findings examine hypertension, blood pressure control, visual acuity, and adulthood factors in relation to cognitive deterioration across three papers. Blood pressure control is linked to slower cognitive decline in two hypertension claims, one of which is worded as a conditional 'might be critical'. Hypertension duration showed no association with cognitive decline, while age at hypertension diagnosis was associated with decline in unclear direction. Worsening visual acuity was associated with cognitive decline, and this is the only claim with a press match, which was aligned. The other five claims have no press match, and no retracted papers appear.

key_findings.text: Blood pressure control was associated with a decrease in cognitive decline, with one paper stating this as a conditional 'might be critical' finding.
Duration of hypertension diagnosis was not associated with any marker of cognitive function decline.
Worsening visual acuity was associated with cognitive deterioration, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
Age at hypertension diagnosis was associated with cognitive decline in different abilities, with the direction unclear.
Adulthood factors explained only 5.6% of the between-person variation in age slope of cognitive change.

reports.title: Mixed exposures and outcomes: COVID-19, depression, cannabidiol, and cognition
reports.summary: This community groups findings on COVID-19 vaccination and severe illness, paternal and maternal depression and offspring depression, cannabidiol and seizure outcomes, ovarian cycle stage and cognitive impairment, and older age across several outcomes. Papers agree that COVID-19 vaccination is associated with lower severe outcomes (C8, C26) and that paternal postnatal depression is associated with offspring depression (C33, C19), although one null result for boys conflicts with this (C28). Conflicts appear for cannabidiol, where one paper says it may reduce seizure frequency (C40) while another finds no difference in seizure freedom (C37), and for ovarian stages, where estrogen-dominant stages are linked to worse cognition (C4) and progesterone-dominant stages to less impairment (C31). Press coverage was mostly aligned with the papers (14 of 17 matched claims), with three overstated (C6, C8, C13) and three understated (C4, C7, C26).

key_findings.text: COVID-19 vaccination was associated with lower severe COVID-19 outcomes, and was reported as effective in dialysis patients at preventing infection and severe outcomes.
Paternal postnatal depression was associated with depression in offspring at age 18, and this association was partly explained by maternal depression.
Cannabidiol may reduce seizure frequency in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, but it showed no statistically significant difference from placebo in seizure freedom.
Estrogen-dominant ovarian cycle stages were reported to worsen cognitive impairment in female mice, while progesterone-dominant stages attenuated these deficits.
Older age was associated with severe COVID-19 and with COVID-19 death in children and young people.

reports.title: COVID-19 Exposures and Outcomes Across Vaccines, Transplant, Neurodegeneration, and Kidney Disease
reports.summary: These findings cover a loosely connected set of studies on COVID-19 and related exposures, including vaccination, donor organ transplant, androgen deprivation therapy, Alzheimer's disease, and chronic kidney disease in cats. Vaccination is linked to lower infection and severe outcomes in dialysis patients, and transplanting SARS-CoV-2 NAT-positive donor organs shows no association with graft loss. The findings conflict on androgen deprivation therapy, where one claim from the same paper reports no effect and another reports a possible decrease in COVID-19. Press labels for the 35 matched claims are mostly aligned (32), with 4 understated and 3 overstated, including the Alzheimer's hippocampal claim C4 and the interferon claim C6. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: COVID-19 vaccination was associated with lower SARS-CoV-2 infection and severe outcomes in the maintenance dialysis population, and one paper states that vaccination is effective despite concerns about antibody responses.
Transplanting organs from SARS-CoV-2 NAT-positive donors showed no association with graft loss, and no donor-derived transmission occurred in the study interval.

Androgen deprivation therapy showed conflicting results within one paper: no effect on COVID-19 in one claim and a possible decrease in another, with any benefit limited to early disease when the virus enters the nasopharynx.

COVID-19 was associated with a higher risk of new Alzheimer's disease diagnosis in older adults, and COVID-19 patients had higher neurofilament light chain, GFAP, and UCHL1 than non-COVID controls with MCI or AD.
Chronic kidney disease in cats was associated with higher serum uremic toxin concentrations and decreased renal tubular transporter gene expression.

reports.title: Smoking associations with prostate cancer, prostate cancer death, and muscle attenuation
reports.summary: This community covers smoking as the exposure, with three outcomes: prostate cancer, prostate cancer death, and lean muscle attenuation. The pooled prostate cancer study (P1) reports smoking associated with lower prostate cancer risk and with increased prostate cancer death, while the CARDIA cohort (P2) reports smoking associated with lower lean muscle attenuation. The directions differ across outcomes rather than between papers on the same outcome, so no direct conflict between papers is stated. Only the prostate cancer risk claim has a press match, which is labeled aligned; the other two claims have no press statement. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Smoking is associated with lower prostate cancer risk in the PSA era, particularly for low-risk prostate cancer, and the paper suggests this probably reflects low PSA testing uptake among smokers.
Smoking is associated with increased prostate cancer death, with poorer survival for smokers, particularly obese smokers.
Smoking is associated with lower lean muscle attenuation in mid-life adults, with current and former smokers both showing lower values than never smokers.

reports.title: Intermittent hypoxia gut microbiota and life stressors linked to sleep disturbance
reports.summary: This community covers two studies that both report sleep disturbance as the outcome, one on gut microbiota changes after intermittent hypoxia and one on life stressors after COVID-19 hospitalization. The mouse study (P1) reports that intermittent hypoxia-induced gut microbiota alterations may increase sleep disturbance, while the COVID-19 cohort (P2) reports that life stressors are associated with increased sleep disturbance. The two papers study different exposures, so they neither conflict nor report opposing directions or null results. For P1, press coverage was mixed: one press statement overstated the paper's strength (press 3 vs paper 2) and another aligned with it (press 2 vs paper 2). No press statement was matched to the life stressors finding in P2, and no retracted papers appear.

key_findings.text: Intermittent hypoxia-induced gut microbiota alterations may increase sleep disturbance in mice, according to P1.
Life stressors are associated with increased sleep disturbance after COVID-19 hospitalization, according to P2.

reports.title: Desulfovibrio bacteria and TFE3 effects on alpha-synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's models
reports.summary: This community covers two studies of alpha-synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's disease models: one on Desulfovibrio bacteria in C. elegans and one on TFE3 in an AAV-alpha-synuclein model. The two papers conflict in direction, since the Desulfovibrio study reports an increase in aggregation (associated with, strength 1) while the TFE3 study reports a decrease (reduces, strength 3). The Desulfovibrio paper also includes a conditional statement that Desulfovibrio may contribute to PD development by inducing aggregation (strength 2). Press coverage of the Desulfovibrio association was overstated in one release and aligned in another, while the TFE3 finding was understated and the conditional Desulfovibrio claim had no press match. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Worms fed Desulfovibrio bacteria from PD patients were associated with more and larger alpha-synuclein aggregates than worms fed healthy-donor Desulfovibrio or E. coli.
TFE3 overexpression reduces alpha-synuclein aggregation.
Desulfovibrio bacteria may contribute to PD development by inducing alpha-syn aggregation.
Press coverage overstated the Desulfovibrio association in one release and understated the TFE3 finding.

reports.title: Exposures and treatments with clinical outcomes across infection, cancer, and COVID-19
reports.summary: This community covers four papers that link treatments or dependence exposures to clinical outcomes in hepatitis C, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, lung cancer screening, and COVID-19. Three claims are associational (strength 1): SVR with improved clinical outcomes, aspirin use with improved outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and high nicotine dependence with worsening clinical outcomes. The ribavirin claim (strength 0) reports no association found and says it is unknown whether adding ribavirin improves outcomes. No two claims point in opposite directions on the same relationship, but the ribavirin null result sits beside the positive associations, although it concerns a different exposure. No press statements were matched to any claim, so press coverage cannot be compared with paper strength, and no retracted papers appear.

key_findings.text: Aspirin use was associated with improved outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
Sustained virologic response after antiviral therapy was associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with no SVR.
Indicators of high nicotine dependence were associated with worsening clinical outcomes in the National Lung Screening Trial.
No association was found for adding ribavirin to early supportive care in Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and the authors state it is not known whether outcomes improve.

reports.title: Oxidative phosphorylation increases in myelodysplastic syndrome and Crimean-Congo fever
reports.summary: The two papers study oxidative phosphorylation as an outcome in myelodysplastic syndrome (P1) and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (P2). Both claims are correlational (strength 1) and both report an increase, so the findings agree in direction and do not conflict. No press statement was matched to either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers' wording.

key_findings.text: In myelodysplastic syndrome, the malignant stem cell compartment is associated with increased oxidative phosphorylation.
During Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus infection, peripheral blood mononuclear cells are associated with upregulated oxidative phosphorylation.

reports.title: Stem cell and Lsd1 approaches targeting medulloblastoma
reports.summary: This community covers medulloblastoma and three exposures or interventions: neural stem cell migration, lysine demethylase 1 (Lsd1), and intra-cavity neural stem cell therapy. P1 reports that neural stem cells are associated with increased migration toward medulloblastoma and that intra-cavity neural stem cell therapy targets residual tumor foci. P2 reports that Lsd1 is associated with medulloblastoma driven by Gfi1, with the direction unclear. The claims in this community do not conflict, and no press statements were matched to any claim, so press coverage cannot be compared. Neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Intra-cavity neural stem cell therapy targets residual medulloblastoma foci after surgical resection in a murine model.
Neural stem cells are associated with increased migration toward medulloblastoma tumors.
Lsd1 is associated with medulloblastoma driven by the transcription factor Gfi1.

reports.title: Interventions targeting LSD1, LRG1, and NMN reducing tumor growth
reports.summary: The three claims examine whether removing or blocking a molecular factor changes tumor growth: LSD1 genetic ablation, LRG1 inhibition, and externally administered NMN. All three report decreased tumor growth, so the papers agree in direction. The strength of wording differs, with P1 and P2 stating direct causal decreases while P3 uses conditional wording for NMN. Only the LRG1 claim (C2) has a matched press statement, labeled aligned, while the LSD1 and NMN claims have no press match. No retracted papers appear and no claims conflict in direction.

key_findings.text: Blocking or removing the factor reduced tumor growth in all three papers, with LSD1 ablation and LRG1 inhibition stated as direct causal decreases.
Genetic ablation of LSD1 reduces tumor growth.
Inhibition of LRG1 reduces tumor growth and improves survival, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.

reports.title: Thrombosis outcomes of macromolecular inhibitors and aspirin use
reports.summary: This community groups two findings that share thrombosis as an outcome: one on macromolecular polyanion inhibitors and one on aspirin use. The polyanion inhibitor paper reports that its lead candidates reduce thrombosis in mouse models without causing bleeding. The aspirin paper, in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, reports no association found between aspirin use and thrombosis, with no difference in overt thrombosis or major bleeding. The two papers study different exposures, so no direct conflict is stated between them. Press coverage matched only the aspirin claim, which was aligned with its paper, while the polyanion inhibitor claim had no press match, so press coverage cannot be compared for it.

key_findings.text: Macromolecular polyanion inhibitors reduce thrombosis in mouse models without causing bleeding.
No association found between aspirin use and overt thrombosis in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with aligned press coverage.

reports.title: Family history of breast cancer and mammography outcomes
reports.summary: This community covers family history of breast cancer as an exposure, linked to screening mammography volume and mammographic density change. P1 found no association between family history and screening mammography volume during the early pandemic period. P2 reports that family history was associated with slightly greater mammographic density reduction. The two papers study different outcomes, so their findings do not directly conflict. No press statements were matched to either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: No association was found between family history of breast cancer and screening mammography volume during the first 5 months of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Family history of breast cancer was associated with slightly greater mammographic density reduction.

reports.title: Medical CT radiation and genetic factors linked to thyroid cancer
reports.summary: These findings study thyroid cancer as the outcome, with medical radiation from CT scans and high- and low-penetrance genetic factors as exposures. P1 reports that CT radiation is associated with thyroid cancer, and that a clear dose-response was seen in patients 45 years or younger. P2 reports that genetic factors may increase thyroid cancer risk through dysregulated hydrogen peroxide metabolism. The two papers do not conflict, since both report increased risk, but they study different exposures. Press coverage matched only the CT finding, where it was aligned with the paper's strength; the genetic finding had no press statement.

key_findings.text: Medical radiation from CT scans is associated with elevated risk of thyroid cancer, with a clear dose-response in patients 45 years or younger.
High- and low-penetrance genetic factors may increase thyroid cancer risk through dysregulated hydrogen peroxide metabolism.

reports.title: CT radiation and F14512 drug effects on non-Hodgkin lymphoma
reports.summary: These findings concern medical radiation from CT scans and the drug F14512 in relation to non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL). The CT study (P1) reports no statistically significant association with NHL in overall patients (C3), while its patients aged 45 years or younger show increased risks, with a dose-response relationship in that group (C1, C4). The dog trial (P2) reports that F14512 reduces NHL compared with etoposide phosphate (C2), so it addresses a different exposure and does not directly conflict with the CT findings. Press coverage is labeled aligned for C2, C3 and C4, while the age-subgroup dose-response claim C1 had no press match.

key_findings.text: In overall patients, CT scan radiation showed no statistically significant association with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
In patients aged 45 years or younger, CT scan radiation was associated with increased non-Hodgkin lymphoma risk, with a clear dose-response relationship.
In dogs with naturally occurring lymphoma, F14512 reduces non-Hodgkin lymphoma compared with etoposide phosphate.

reports.title: Palliative care, aspirin, and behavioral health links to hospital and ICU outcomes
reports.summary: This community covers four papers linking palliative care, aspirin use, and behavioral health disorders to outcomes such as mechanical ventilation, readmission, ICU admission, mortality, and family-rated end-of-life care. All six claims are correlational, worded as 'associated with' (strength 1), and none makes a direct causal claim. The palliative care claims from P1 report lower mechanical ventilation, lower readmission, and fewer defibrillator implantations, while the P4 claim reports higher family ratings of end-of-life care. No exposure-outcome pair has opposing directions across papers, so there is no direct conflict. Press labels mark the P1 and P3 claims as overstated and the P1 through P4 claims as aligned in some cases, with P1 claims carrying both labels.

key_findings.text: Palliative care consultation was associated with fewer multiple readmissions and less mechanical ventilation in P1.
Aspirin use was associated with decreased mechanical ventilation, ICU admission, and in-hospital mortality in hospitalized patients (P3).
Behavioral health disorders were associated with higher odds of readmission in surgical cancer patients (P2).
Palliative care and hospice services were associated with higher family ratings of end-of-life care for veterans with advanced CKD (P4).
Palliative care was associated with a lower rate of defibrillator implantation in P1.

reports.title: Parkinson's disease linked to sleep problems and Desulfovibrio gut bacteria
reports.summary: The findings center on Parkinson's disease (PD), studied alongside two other topics: sleep problems in PD patients and Desulfovibrio bacteria. A 2025 study of PD patients reports that insomnia, restless legs syndrome, vivid dreams, acting out dreams, and sleep medication use are associated with PD compared with matched healthy controls. A 2023 Caenorhabditis elegans study suggests that Desulfovibrio bacteria may contribute to PD development by promoting alpha-synuclein aggregation. All six claims point in the same direction (increase), and the sleep findings are correlational, so no papers conflict. For press coverage, the Desulfovibrio claim had one press statement labelled overstated and one labelled aligned, while the sleep medication claim was labelled aligned and the other sleep claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: Patients with Parkinson's disease show higher rates of insomnia, restless legs syndrome, vivid dreams, acting out dreams, and sleep medication use, each associated with PD.
Desulfovibrio bacteria may contribute to Parkinson's disease development by inducing alpha-synuclein aggregation.
Press coverage of the sleep medication finding was aligned with the paper's strength.

reports.title: Autophagy induction by spermidine, felodipine, TFE3 and vaccination
reports.summary: These four papers study autophagy as the shared outcome, with exposures including spermidine, felodipine, TFE3 overexpression, and vaccination. All seven claims report increases in the same direction, so no papers conflict and no null results appear. Spermidine, vaccination, felodipine and TFE3 are each stated as increasing autophagy at strength 3, autophagy is only associated with interferon-gamma secretion at strength 1, and vaccination may accelerate COVID-19 endemicity at strength 2. Press coverage matched the paper's strength for four of the five matched claims, while the felodipine claim was understated (press 2 vs paper 3). Two claims, autophagy with interferon-gamma and vaccination with endemicity, had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Spermidine increases autophagy, and endogenous spermidine maintains autophagy via eIF5A and TFEB.
Vaccination increases autophagy in vaccine-induced antigen-specific CD8+ T cells in healthy volunteers.
Felodipine increases autophagy and clears aggregate-prone disease-associated proteins, and TFE3 overexpression increases autophagy and reduces α-synuclein aggregation.
Autophagy is associated with interferon-gamma secretion by T cells in older vaccinees.
Vaccination may accelerate the establishment of a state of mild COVID-19 endemicity.

reports.title: Regulatory T cells in cancer immunotherapy and cardiac remodeling
reports.summary: This community covers regulatory T cells (Tregs) in two unrelated settings: a CSF1R inhibitor combined with cisplatin in genetically engineered lung cancer models (P1), and Tregs in chronic ischemic heart failure (P2). The two papers study different exposures and outcomes, so their findings do not agree or conflict with each other. The CSF1R inhibitor plus cisplatin finding is stated with direct causal wording in P1, and the Treg finding is stated with direct causal wording in P2. Both claims are labelled aligned in press coverage, meaning press statements matched the strength of the papers' own wording, and neither is labelled overstated or understated.

key_findings.text: In lung cancer models, a CSF1R inhibitor plus cisplatin reduces regulatory T cells.
In chronic ischemic heart failure, regulatory T cells increase and play an essential pathogenetic role in pathological left ventricular remodeling.

reports.title: Progesterone exposure and endothelial dysfunction, mineralocorticoid receptor, and meningioma risk
reports.summary: This community covers progesterone as the shared exposure, with endothelial dysfunction and intracranial meningioma as outcomes, drawn from two papers. One study in female mice reports that progesterone increases endothelial mineralocorticoid receptor expression and is associated with leptin-induced endothelial dysfunction. A national case-control study found no association between progesterone and intracranial meningioma. The two papers examine different outcomes, so they do not directly conflict. Only the meningioma null finding has a press match, and its press statement was aligned with the paper; the endothelial claims have no press match.

key_findings.text: Progesterone increases endothelial mineralocorticoid receptor expression in female mice.
Progesterone is associated with leptin-induced endothelial dysfunction.
No association was found between progesterone and intracranial meningioma.

reports.title: Recurrence links to genetic pathway burden and SOX9 in brain tumours
reports.summary: This community covers recurrence in glioblastoma and medulloblastoma, linking recurrence to genetic pathway alterations and to SOX9 expression. Two claims from one glioblastoma paper associate recurrent tumours with fewer genetic pathways impacted. The medulloblastoma paper reports that SOX9 facilitates recurrence through temporal inhibition of MYC/MYCN genes. The findings address different exposures, so no direction conflict appears among them. Press coverage matched only the SOX9 claim, which carries both overstated and understated labels, so the press comparison is unclear. The glioblastoma claims have no press match.

key_findings.text: Recurrent tumours are associated with fewer genetic pathways impacted, including p53, WNT, and G-protein pathways.
SOX9 expression facilitates recurrence in medulloblastoma via temporal inhibition of MYC/MYCN genes.

reports.title: Low income linked to mortality after CABG and reduced muscle-strengthening exercise
reports.summary: This community centers on low income as an exposure, linked to two outcomes: all-cause mortality and sufficient muscle-strengthening exercise. In P1, the lowest income quintile compared with the highest was associated with higher all-cause mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting, with a larger hazard ratio in men than in women. P2 reports that low income was associated with a lower likelihood of reporting sufficient muscle-strengthening exercise, alongside older age, being female, and being overweight or obese. The two papers study different outcomes, so no conflicting results between them were found. The mortality finding in P1 is aligned with its press statement, while the exercise finding in P2 has no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Low income was associated with higher all-cause mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting, with a hazard ratio of 1.44 in men and 1.25 in women.
Low income was associated with a lower likelihood of reporting sufficient muscle-strengthening exercise.

reports.title: Low education and outcomes: mortality after CABG and muscle-strengthening exercise
reports.summary: This community covers low education as an exposure, linked to all-cause mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting and to sufficient muscle-strengthening exercise. Each relationship comes from a single paper, and the mortality finding was reported as associated with higher risk, without a sex difference. The two papers study different populations and outcomes, so the community shows no agreement or conflict between them. Press coverage was matched only for the mortality finding, where it was aligned with the paper's strength. The exercise finding had no matched press statement, and neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Lowest education level was associated with higher risk of all-cause mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Lower education was associated with a lower likelihood of reporting sufficient muscle-strengthening exercise among European adults.

reports.title: Physical activity, brain gray matter volume, and open classroom learning spaces
reports.summary: The findings study physical activity and sedentary behavior in relation to brain structure and to classroom learning environments. P1 reports that moderate-to-vigorous physical activity is associated with greater total gray matter volume, with the relation leveling off at higher activity levels. P2 reports that open learning spaces may facilitate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity among elementary students compared with conventional classrooms. The two claims concern different exposures and outcomes, so the papers neither agree nor conflict. Neither claim has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity is associated with greater total gray matter volume, though the relation levels off with more activity.
Open learning spaces may facilitate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity among elementary school students compared with conventional classrooms.

reports.title: Synthetic torpor and intravascular immune activation linked to lung damage
reports.summary: The two findings concern lung damage in different settings: one study examines 5′-AMP treatment in rats exposed to heavy-ion radiation, and the other links intravascular innate immune system activation to organ damage in critically ill COVID-19 patients. The findings do not address the same exposure, so they neither agree nor conflict. The rat study reports a direct causal reduction in lung damage with 5′-AMP treatment, while the COVID-19 study reports only an association between immune activation and lung damage. Both findings were aligned with their press coverage, so press statements matched the strength of the papers' wording.

key_findings.text: 5′-AMP treatment following radiation exposure reduced lung damage in rats.
Intravascular innate immune system activation is associated with lung damage in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

reports.title: Diet, psychological profiles, and synthetic cannabinoid effects on cognitive performance
reports.summary: The three findings share cognitive performance as an outcome but link it to different exposures: a spaceflight diet, a psychological profile, and a synthetic cannabinoid. The enhanced spaceflight diet is associated with increased cognitive performance, while the low protective psychological profile is associated with decreased cognitive performance. JWH-018 is reported to impair cognition, mainly in participants who experienced subjective intoxication. No two claims address the same exposure-outcome pair in opposite directions. Press coverage was aligned for C1 and C2 and overstated for C3.

key_findings.text: The enhanced spaceflight diet is associated with increased cognitive performance, including better speed, accuracy, and attention.
A low protective psychological profile is associated with decreased cognitive performance, with the worst objective cognition in older and middle age.
JWH-018 impairs cognition and subjective measures, mainly in participants who experienced subjective intoxication, and press coverage of this finding was overstated.

reports.title: Hypertension and snoring associated with cognitive decline and uncontrolled hypertension
reports.summary: This community covers two papers: one studying hypertension as an exposure to lower global cognitive and memory test scores, and one studying regular snoring as an exposure to uncontrolled hypertension. All five claims are correlational (strength 1), so they state that hypertension was associated with lower cognitive scores and that snoring was associated with uncontrolled hypertension, not that either causes the other. The claims about the hypertension paper agree in direction, all showing decreases in cognitive or memory scores, and no claim reports a null result or an opposing direction. Press coverage differs by claim: the hypertension and global cognitive score claim was labelled overstated (press strength 2 against paper strength 1), the snoring and hypertension claim was aligned, and the memory test claims had no matched press statement. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Hypertension was associated with decline in global cognitive score in the baseline analysis.
Hypertension diagnosed at age 55 or older, and hypertension diagnosed under 55, were each associated with lower memory test scores.
A higher proportion of time spent snoring was associated with about a 1.9-fold increase in uncontrolled hypertension, independent of sleep apnea.
Press coverage overstated the association between hypertension and global cognitive score, while the snoring and hypertension finding was reported in line with the paper.

reports.title: Cervical cancer exposures and outcomes: olaparib concentration, toxicity, CIN2 surveillance
reports.summary: The findings cover two topics linked by cervical cancer: olaparib concentration and toxicity in cancer cells (P1), and the long-term cervical cancer risk of untreated CIN2 (P2). For untreated CIN2, the BMJ cohort reports active surveillance as associated with increased long-term cervical cancer risk, while also reporting no association over the two-year surveillance period, so the two claims differ in time frame rather than direction. The olaparib paper reports that cervical cancer cells are associated with higher intracellular olaparib concentration and a lower toxic effect, with no press coverage matched to either claim. Both CIN2 claims were matched to press coverage and labelled aligned, meaning the press statements matched the strength of the papers' wording.

key_findings.text: Active surveillance of CIN2 is associated with increased long-term risk of cervical cancer compared with immediate LLETZ.
Cumulative cervical cancer risk showed no association between active surveillance and immediate treatment during the two-year surveillance period.
Cervical cancer cells are associated with a tenfold higher intracellular olaparib concentration than breast cancer cells.
Cervical cancer cells are associated with a lower olaparib toxic effect than breast cancer cells.

reports.title: Dementia, mood and fatigue outcomes across fitness, marital status, loneliness and sex
reports.summary: The claims study dementia risk in relation to cardiorespiratory fitness, marital status, loneliness, and recorded memory concerns, alongside mood, fatigue, and sex-related exposures in clinical and population settings. Several papers agree that higher or sustained cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with lower dementia risk, and that unmarried status and loneliness are associated with higher dementia risk. Women are linked to higher outcome or prevalence measures in several papers, but the no-effect claim from P15 reports no evidence of systematic under-representation of women in trials, and P17 associates female sex with lower muscle-strengthening exercise. Press coverage is mostly aligned with paper strength, but overstated labels appear for P1 fitness claims, P7 marital status, P3, and P5. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Higher or sustained cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with reduced dementia incidence and mortality in P1, and maintaining or improving fitness may be a target to reduce dementia risk.
Unmarried status, including divorced, widowed, and never-married groups, is associated with higher odds of dementia than being married in P7.
Loneliness is associated with higher 10-year dementia risk in P8, with the strongest reported effect in lonely participants under 80 without APOE ε4 alleles.
Women and people in more deprived areas with recorded memory concerns or cognitive decline are more likely to progress to dementia in P2.
Female sex is associated with higher anxiety, fatigue, and nonacceptance of statin therapy in P3, P4, P6, and P10, while P15 reports no evidence of systematic under-representation of women in trials.

reports.title: Aging-Associated Changes in Hair, Intestinal Epithelium, and T-Cell Spermidine
reports.summary: These three papers study how aging relates to biological changes in mouse hair, intestinal epithelium, and human T cells. Two claims report decreases with age: intestinal regenerative potential (P2) and spermidine levels in T cells (P3), each at correlational strength, so they agree in direction but do not show causation. The hair study (P1) reports age-related hair phenotypes in mice with an unclear direction, so it cannot be compared with the others. No findings conflict in direction, and no paper in this community is retracted. Press coverage of the intestinal finding was labeled understated, the T-cell spermidine finding was labeled aligned, and the hair finding had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Aging is associated with a decrease in the regenerative potential of human and mouse intestinal epithelium.
Aging is associated with a decrease in the endogenous autophagy-inducing metabolite spermidine in human T cells.
Aging, along with endocrinological and developmental changes, is reported to be associated with hair phenotypes in mice, though the direction of the effect is unclear.

reports.title: Long COVID immune dysregulation and life stressors after SARS-CoV-2 infection
reports.summary: The two papers study long COVID alongside immune features (T cell, antibody and inflammation markers) in one paper and life stressors and COVID-19 severity in the other. Both papers' claims are correlational, with each relationship worded as associated with the outcome. The papers do not report conflicting directions, and the T cell subset findings are described as unclear. Press coverage matched the paper for most immune claims, but the press overstated the link between COVID-19 severity and long COVID, and four claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: Long COVID is associated with increased exhaustion of SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cells, higher SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels and increased CD4+ T cell frequency.
Life stressors, including financial insecurity, food insecurity, death of a close contact and new disability, are associated with long COVID, with adjusted odds ratios from 2.5 to 20.8.
Long COVID is associated with systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation.
Greater COVID-19 severity is associated with long COVID, although press coverage overstated this link.
The link between long COVID and T cell subset distribution, cytolytic subsets, and coordination between SARS-CoV-2-specific T and B cell responses is unclear.

reports.title: Nanobody multimerization and paratope mutation effects on binding affinity
reports.summary: These findings study how nanobody multimerization and a single paratope mutation affect binding affinity. One paper reports that multimerization increases affinity, with divalent and higher-order oligomers reaching sub-nanomolar affinity. The other paper finds no association between paratope mutation and binding affinity, while reporting roughly 30 times faster dissociation rates. The two claims address different exposures, so they do not directly conflict. No press statements were matched to either paper, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Nanobody multimerization increases binding affinity, with divalent and higher-order oligomers reaching sub-nanomolar affinity.
No association was found between targeting a single paratope and binding affinity, although dissociation rates were about 30 times faster than wild type.

reports.title: Amyloid-β and neuronal hyperexcitability in Alzheimer's disease models
reports.summary: This community covers amyloid-β (Aβ) and neuronal hyperexcitability, with one study on neuritin (NRN1) as a possible protective factor. P1 reports that NRN1 blocked Aβ-induced hyperexcitability in cultured neurons, a direct causal wording at strength 3. P2 reports only a correlation, with Aβ deposition in the mammillary body associated with neuronal hyper-excitability in mice, at strength 1. The two claims study different exposures, so they do not directly contradict each other. Both claims carry press statements labelled aligned, meaning press wording matched the strength of the paper's wording. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: NRN1 blocked Aβ-induced neuronal hyperexcitability in cultured neurons, a direct causal decrease in the paper's wording.
Aβ deposition in the mammillary body was associated with neuronal hyper-excitability in mice, a correlational finding.

reports.title: Hydroxychloroquine exposure and mortality, mechanical ventilation, and SLC19A3 transport
reports.summary: This community centers on hydroxychloroquine as the shared exposure, studied against all-cause mortality and mechanical ventilation in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and against thiamine transporter SLC19A3 activity in a structural study. In the COVID-19 retrospective study (P1), hydroxychloroquine was associated with higher all-cause mortality in the hydroxychloroquine group, while no association was found for mechanical ventilation or for death after ventilation. The same paper's summary statement reports no significant reduction in mortality or ventilation need, which conflicts in direction with the mortality association. The SLC19A3 paper (P2) associates hydroxychloroquine with decreased transporter activity, and it has no press match. Both P1 claims with press matches were aligned with press coverage, and no retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Hydroxychloroquine was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with no hydroxychloroquine, although this was not seen in the hydroxychloroquine plus azithromycin group.
No association was found between hydroxychloroquine and mechanical ventilation use or death after mechanical ventilation.
The retrospective study did not identify any significant reduction in mortality or in the need for mechanical ventilation with hydroxychloroquine, with or without azithromycin.
Hydroxychloroquine was associated with decreased activity of the thiamine transporter SLC19A3.

reports.title: Lifestyle and liver-gut neural factors in MAFLD and NAFLD development
reports.summary: These findings study lifestyle exposures (alcohol intake, late-night meals, meal frequency) and a hepatic neural axis, with steatotic liver disease as the shared outcome. P1 and P2 report positive links between their exposures and fatty liver disease, while P1 finds no lifestyle association in participants aged 60 or older, a null result beside its positive findings for younger participants. P3 reports only an association between NAFLD and glucagonotropic amino acids such as alanine, and P2 describes the liver-gut axis as involved without stating a direction. Press coverage was mostly aligned with paper strength, with one claim overstated (C4) and one understated (C5).

key_findings.text: Alcohol intake, late-night meals, and meal frequency were each associated with MAFLD development in P1.
Hepatic neural blockade and HTR2A antagonist treatment reduced NAFLD progression in P2.
P2 reports that the autonomic liver-gut neural axis is involved in diet-induced NAFLD, with no stated direction of effect.
NAFLD was associated with hyperglucagonemia and increased glucagonotropic amino acids, including alanine, in P3.
No lifestyle habits were associated with MAFLD development in participants aged 60 or older in P1.

reports.title: mtFIT screening and lamivudine in colorectal cancer outcomes
reports.summary: This community covers colorectal cancer, linking mtFIT-based stool screening and lamivudine (3TC) to colorectal cancer outcomes across two papers. The papers study different exposures, a screening strategy and a reverse transcriptase inhibitor, so their findings do not directly conflict. The Dutch mtFIT study's modelling reports that mtFIT-based screening may reduce colorectal cancer incidence and mortality compared with the current programme, and that it reduces incidence and mortality further compared with FIT-based screening. The lamivudine study is associated with an increase in colorectal cancer, and press coverage of it was overstated relative to the paper. Press coverage of the mtFIT screening findings was aligned with the paper for the main comparison, and the FIT comparison had no press match.

key_findings.text: mtFIT-based screening may reduce colorectal cancer incidence by 21% and associated mortality by 18% compared with the current Dutch screening programme, at feasible costs.
At an equally low positivity rate, mtFIT-based screening reduces colorectal cancer incidence by 5% and associated mortality by 4% compared with FIT-based screening.
Lamivudine is associated with an increase in colorectal cancer in a repeat element study, and press coverage overstated this finding.

reports.title: Lynch gene variants and breast cancer; PRS and mammographic density features
reports.summary: The findings cover germline variants in Lynch syndrome genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) and breast cancer risk, from one paper, and a genetic predisposition to breast cancer (PRS) and mammographic breast density features, from a second paper. Within the Lynch study, MSH6 and PMS2 variants are associated with breast cancer, while MLH1 and MSH2 show no association found, so the genes do not agree. The mammographic study reports a positive association between genetic predisposition and breast density and microcalcifications, with masses only borderline significant. Both associations that have a press match are labelled aligned, and the other claims have no press match. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: MSH6 and PMS2 germline variants are associated with breast cancer.
No association was found between MLH1 or MSH2 germline variants and breast cancer.
Genetic predisposition to breast cancer is associated with mammographic breast density and microcalcifications.
Genetic predisposition to breast cancer is associated with mammographic masses, but only at borderline significance.
